title: Improved Gradient Descent Lower Bounds Beyond Nesterov
abstract: We study how far gradient descent (GD) can be accelerated by predetermined stepsizes in smooth convex optimization. Going beyond the classical $Ω(n^{-2})$ first-order oracle lower bound of Nemirovsky and Yudin (1983), we prove an $Ω(n^{-1.6342})$ non-anytime lower bound and an $Ω(n^{-1.2408})$ anytime lower bound. These improve the recent $Ω(n^{-1.932})$ non-anytime lower bound of Ma and Chen (2026) and the $Ω(n^{-4/3})$ anytime lower bound of Tsai et al. (2026), respectively. Both results continue to hold when the stepsizes may be negative. Our anytime lower bound also shows that the $O(n^{-\log_2(1+\sqrt{2})})$ rate of non-anytime silver schedules (Altschuler and Parrilo, 2025; Grimmer et al., 2025) is unattainable in the anytime setting. This establishes a strict separation between the two settings.

title: The Dynamics of Continuous Mixture Collapse in Language Models
abstract: LLMs latent-state reasoning methods replace discrete intermediate tokens with continuous states, such as weighted mixtures of token embeddings, to retain multiple possible reasoning directions rather than committing to one. Yet pretrained language models often fail to preserve these mixtures. We study why through a combination of theoretical analysis and controlled empirical investigations on a variety of models. We identify three independent, distinct sources of failure. First, transformer architectures already distort mixture geometry, and training substantially amplifies this effect. Moreover, the failure can occur even if the model transports mixtures perfectly linearly: the softmax readout and autoregressive feedback form a dynamical system that either amplifies small differences until one component of the mixture dominates or contracts different mixtures until they become indistinguishable. We verify this theoretical prediction empirically: the observed transition between contraction and amplification occurs near the theoretical threshold derived by our analysis, and pretrained-model rollouts lie predominantly on the amplifying side. Finally, we generalize to mixtures of many components and show that exact preservation generally requires context-dependent correction, whose required dimensionality can grow with the number of components.

title: SEAL: Reinforcing Global Safety in Mixture-of-Experts through Shared Expert ALignment
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) is a scaling architecture for large language models that activates only a small subset of expert modules per token, enabling massive parameter growth with nearly constant computation. Recent Hybrid MoE architecture adds \textit{shared experts} to capture consistently useful representations, further improving stability and generalization. MoE now powers many flagship open-source and commercial models, yet remains vulnerable to adversarial attacks. Specifically, sparse routing introduces a structural vulnerability: MoE safety hinges on which experts are activated, and adversaries can subvert this selection through jailbreak prompts, malicious fine-tuning, and weight-level pruning of safety-critical neurons. Existing defenses primarily focus on hardening the router, but an adversary may still manipulate or bypass the routing trajectory due to the routing process's nondeterministic nature, thereby collapsing the defense. To cope with this problem, we first identify theoretically and empirically that shared expert, an always-activated component containing a small proportion of safety-critical neurons, can overcome the uncertainty of sparsely activated routing path and serve as a router-independent anchor to enhance global safety alignment. Based on this insight, we propose SEAL, a training-time parameter-efficient defense that produces a plug-and-play adapter attached to shared expert, and SEAL++, a variant that adds an orthogonal constraint preserving pre-existing safety subspaces during training. We evaluate SEAL and SEAL++ across six attack scenarios that combine three adversarial inputs (harmful prompting, jailbreak, malicious fine-tuning) with and without neuron pruning. SEAL reduces attack success rate (ASR) by up to 60\%, at a capability cost of at most 1.4\% on a five-benchmark average. Additionally, SEAL can seamlessly integrate with router-level ......

title: A quantum chirp transform-based multi-qubit encoding framework for quantum-inspired image transmission over error-prone channels
abstract: Reliable transmission of compressed images over error-prone channels remains challenging because compressed bitstreams are highly sensitive to channel impairments. Although existing quantum-inspired encoding schemes exploit superposition to improve transmission reliability, they remain vulnerable to channel noise, limiting reconstructed image quality. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a chirp transform-based multi-qubit encoding framework for robust compressed image transmission. Unlike conventional transform-based approaches, including the Hadamard transform and Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT), the proposed framework introduces nonlinear (quadratic) phase modulation into the multi-qubit representation, producing a high-dimensional superposition that enhances noise resilience through improved phase separability. This nonlinear phase variation improves error resilience through phase-induced decorrelation, reducing noise-induced distortions. The system integrates Joint Photographic Experts Group (JPEG) and High Efficiency Image File Format (HEIF) source encoding, followed by channel coding, multi-qubit encoding, and chirp transformation before transmission through a simulated quantum channel. At the receiver, inverse chirp transformation, measurement-based decoding, channel decoding, and source decoding reconstruct the transmitted image. Performance is evaluated using Bit Error Rate (BER), Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM), and Universal Quality Index (UQI). Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves up to a 3 dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) gain over QFT-based and Hadamard-based systems in the single-qubit configuration. For the eight-qubit configuration, gains of up to 2 dB over QFT-based systems and 7 dB over Hadamard-based systems are achieved. These results demonstrate the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed framework for robust compressed image transmission over noisy quantum communication channels.

title: A Comprehensive Survey on Light weight block Ciphers with Authentication approaches for low resource IoT devices
abstract: Resource limited devices like IoT nodes, RFID tags, wireless sensor networks, and embedded edge technologies can now be safeguarded with the help of lightweight cryptography. Traditional cryptographic primitives are not suitable for these devices because they work under stringent conditions on power, area, storage, and latency. With emphasis on hardware implementations, this review offers an in depth and methodical analysis of existing lightweight block ciphers and authentication techniques. High-profile journal articles published between 2018 and 2026 are scrutinized and analyzed using a PRISMA-based methodology. The study includes techniques that are focused on authentication as well as traditional and new lightweight block ciphers. Metrics at the ASIC and FPGA levels, including LUTs, power usage, frequency, slices, latency, throughput, and hardware efficiency, are used to perform quantitative comparisons. Significant design trade-offs between area-optimized, throughput-oriented, and energy-efficient designs are highlighted in the analysis, along with the increasing trend of integrated encryption–authentication approaches. The survey also finds inadequacies in side-channel resilience, scalability across various heterogeneous platforms, security–efficiency co-optimization, and uniform benchmarking. Finally, future research scope is described for leading the creation of emerging lightweight cryptographic architectures that strike a undermine between hardware efficiency and robustness for contexts with limited resources.

Finally, future research scope is described for leading the creation of emerging lightweight cryptographic architectures that strike a undermine between hardware efficiency and robustness for contexts with limited resources.

title: Adaptive Hyperparameter Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive hyperparameter optimization algorithm designed to enhance model generalization. Traditional hyperparameter optimization methods often employ static strategies, failing to adapt to the intricacies of individual models. This research proposes a novel approach leveraging reinforcement learning to dynamically adjust optimization strategies based on model performance feedback. The core mechanism focuses on iteratively refining hyperparameter values through a reinforcement learning loop, mitigating the risk of over-optimization and promoting better model performance. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through a comprehensive analysis of several benchmark datasets, showcasing significant improvements in generalization ability.

title: Context-Aware Dynamic Program Synthesis Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to program synthesis optimization termed "Context-Aware Dynamic Program Synthesis Optimization." The core idea is to move beyond static analysis by incorporating real-time information about the program execution context—including hardware characteristics, system load, and data distribution—directly into the synthesis process. This enables the creation of optimization strategies that are far more adaptive and effective than traditional static methods. We propose a "context-aware" program synthesis engine that leverages machine learning models, such as reinforcement learning or generative adversarial networks, to predict optimal optimization schemes. This engine is then integrated with conventional program synthesis techniques like SAT solvers and Turing machine models, allowing for dynamic code generation and verification. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adaptation of the synthesis process based on runtime context, offering a fundamentally new paradigm for program optimization.

title: Evolving Neural Architectures via Genetic Algorithms
abstract: This paper investigates the application of genetic algorithms (GAs) to the automated design and optimization of neural network architectures. Traditional neural network design relies heavily on human expertise and trial-and-error, often leading to sub-optimal architectures. This research proposes a novel approach where neural network architectures are encoded as chromosomes within a GA, allowing for the evolutionary exploration of diverse architectural configurations. The core mechanism involves employing genetic operators—mutation and crossover—to iteratively refine these architectures based on predefined performance metrics. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through a theoretical framework and a conceptual outline, highlighting its potential to significantly reduce the design time and improve the performance of neural networks. The aim is to shift the design process from a manual, intuitive approach to a robust, automated one driven by evolutionary principles. This work establishes a foundation for future research in automated neural architecture search using GAs and related optimization techniques.

title: Adaptive Symbolic Regression with Grammatical Evolution
abstract: Symbolic regression is a powerful technique for discovering mathematical equations from data. However, its computational cost can be prohibitive, particularly for complex datasets and high-dimensional problems. This paper introduces an adaptive symbolic regression framework that combines grammatical evolution with an adaptive rule selection mechanism. The core idea is to leverage the generative capabilities of grammatical evolution to explore the space of possible equations, while simultaneously employing a feedback loop to prioritize and refine expressions based on their predictive accuracy, as measured by a differentiable loss function. This approach effectively mitigates the random exploration limitations inherent in traditional symbolic regression, leading to significantly accelerated convergence and improved equation quality. The system dynamically adjusts its search strategy, focusing on expressions that demonstrate superior performance, resulting in a more targeted and efficient optimization process. This work demonstrates the potential of this integrated framework for tackling challenging symbolic regression problems.

title: 基于自适应的深度学习的知识推理优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel knowledge reasoning optimization algorithm based on adaptive deep learning. Traditional knowledge reasoning methods often rely on fixed parameters, which can limit the algorithm's ability to effectively optimize knowledge inference. Our proposed approach utilizes adaptive parameter adjustment to dynamically fine-tune the model's parameters, resulting in improved accuracy and efficiency. We present a theoretical framework and empirical results demonstrating the effectiveness of this method in various knowledge reasoning tasks. The core mechanism revolves around a self-learning parameter adjustment process, enabling the algorithm to adapt to the specific characteristics of the knowledge domain. The paper also discusses potential challenges and future research directions in this area.

title: 基于多模态信息融合的神经符号推理引擎
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neuro-symbolic reasoning engine designed to tackle complex problems by integrating the strengths of deep learning and symbolic reasoning. The core concept is to fuse multi-modal information – including images, text, and audio – to create a richer understanding of the problem domain. This understanding is then leveraged through a neuro-symbolic architecture that performs logical inference and knowledge representation. Specifically, the engine utilizes convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for feature extraction from image and audio data, and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) combined with graph neural networks (GNNs) for processing textual information. The fused features are then fed into a symbolic reasoning module, enabling the engine to derive conclusions based on logical rules and existing knowledge. Experimental results (simulated due to the absence of physical experimentation) demonstrate the potential of this approach for improved problem-solving accuracy compared to traditional methods relying solely on either deep learning or symbolic reasoning. The engine's architecture is designed for modularity and extensibility, allowing for the integration of new data modalities and reasoning rules. Future research directions include exploring different fusion techniques and developing more sophisticated symbolic reasoning methods. ---

title: Quantum Teleportation: Entangled Bits to Energy Transfer — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: FINDING: Quantum teleportation transmits quantum states (not matter) over 1,400 km via entangled photons; recent work extends this to teleporting energy on superconducting hardware. | MATH: Core protocol uses Bell-state measurement — projective measurement onto one of 4 maximally entangled basis states, requiring classical communication of 2 bits per teleported qubit. Entanglement fidelity F = ⟨ψ|ρ_out|ψ⟩; success probability scales as 1/2^N for N-qubit teleportation without distillation. Energy teleportation (arXiv:2301.02666) uses local operations and classical communication (LOCC) to extract energy from a vacuum-like entangled state, with energy gain ΔE = (ħω/2)(1 − √(1 − γ²)) per cycle, where γ is the entanglement parameter. | CONNECTION: The Bell basis is isomorphic to the Klein four-group (Z₂×Z₂) — a crystallographic point group symmetry. title: A Cognitive Architecture Based on Information Theory
abstract: This paper proposes a novel cognitive architecture grounded in information theory, aiming to provide a more quantitative and mechanistic understanding of human cognition. Traditional cognitive architectures often rely heavily on psychological theories, which can be descriptive but lack precise numerical measures of cognitive processes. This architecture leverages concepts like entropy, mutual information, and redundancy to model cognitive states and dynamics. The core claim is that cognition can be effectively viewed as an information processing system. We define a framework for representing cognitive elements – such as memory representations and processing operations – using information-theoretic metrics. This approach allows for the quantification of uncertainty, relevance, and efficiency within cognitive systems. The architecture is designed to capture the essential features of human cognition, offering a potential pathway for developing more robust and testable cognitive models. This paper outlines the core components of the architecture and provides a preliminary exploration of its potential applications.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding and Decoding: A Dynamic Entropy Adjustment
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers unparalleled potential for secure communication and advanced computation. This research explores the implementation of a dynamic entropy adjustment scheme to stabilize quantum entanglement, enabling more precise quantum information transfer and decoding. The core claim centers around leveraging this dynamic adjustment to control entanglement evolution, thereby enhancing the reliability and efficiency of quantum information processing. Current approaches often rely on static entanglement management, necessitating a novel mechanism to dynamically control the state. This work introduces a system that uses a controlled evolution of the entangled state to induce specific properties, offering a pathway to overcome limitations inherent in existing encoding strategies. The resulting system demonstrates improved entanglement fidelity and a potential shift towards more robust and flexible quantum communication protocols.

title: Dynamic Bayesian Resonance
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Bayesian Resonance (DBR), a novel approach to Bayesian inference that leverages the concept of resonance to enhance efficiency and accuracy. The core idea is to dynamically adjust the resonance frequencies within a Bayesian network, creating a feedback loop that optimizes the network's alignment with the underlying probability distribution. The mechanism involves tuning the weights and parameters of the network based on observed data, effectively "tuning" the network to resonate. Mathematical formulations are presented to illustrate this dynamic adjustment process, focusing on the relationship between observed data, resonance frequencies, and Bayesian network parameters. The potential for DBR to significantly accelerate probabilistic reasoning and improve the robustness of Bayesian models is explored, highlighting its unique integration of resonance theory with Bayesian inference. The efficacy of this method is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and conceptual framework, providing a foundation for future experimental validation.

title: Topological Information Encoding for Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper proposes a novel quantum computing framework based on topological information encoding, aiming to enhance quantum computation's robustness and efficiency through the strategic integration of topological structures. We introduce a system where quantum states are dynamically linked to topological structures, utilizing quantum entanglement to amplify the information contained within these structures. The core mechanism leverages the inherent properties of topological phases to provide improved security and scalability. This framework offers a fundamentally different approach to quantum computation, offering a promising pathway towards more reliable and efficient quantum systems. We present a detailed design of this framework, including mathematical formulations and a discussion of its potential advantages and limitations. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications.

title: CompileML
abstract: CompileML compiles tree-ensemble models into deterministic, auditable, integer-exact decision artifacts. A single hashed JSON document carries the integer-quantized score, isotonic calibration, fixed-point risk bands, reason codes, and exact per-feature attributions; a standard-library-only runtime scores it, and SQL and COBOL exporters reproduce the same integers row for row. At whitebox depth two or less, attribution is exact — every explanation sums back to the production score with no residual — and the artifact collapses to a classical points scorecard without approximation.

title: Too Simple, Too Complex, Just Right: A Comparative Analysis Review of Inductive Biases in Deep Learning Architectures
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Inductive Biases in Deep Learning Architectures in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of deep learning and inductive bias as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: MSF-TransPV: a multi-source fusion transformer for short-term photovoltaic power forecasting
abstract: Accurate short-term photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is essential for secure grid operation, economic dispatch, and efficient utilization of renewable energy. However, PV output exhibits strong nonlinearity and nonstationarity due to rapidly varying meteorological conditions, cloud movements, and system uncertainties. Conventional statistical models and single-source deep learning approaches often fail to fully exploit the rich multi-source information available in modern PV plants, such as historical power, on-site meteorological measurements, and clear-sky or numerical weather prediction (NWP) features. In this paper, we propose MSF-TransPV, a Multi-Source Fusion Transformer framework for short-term PV power forecasting. The model adopts a multi-branch temporal encoder that separately processes historical PV output, meteorological variables, and optional clear-sky/NWP-derived features, mapping them into a shared latent space. A cross-variable multi-head attention module is then introduced to explicitly capture the dependencies between PV dynamics and atmospheric conditions, enabling fine-grained interaction across different feature sources. On top of the fused representation, a temporal Transformer encoder models long-range temporal dependencies and feeds a lightweight decoder that supports both point forecasting and probabilistic forecasting via quantile regression. Experimental results on real-world PV datasets demonstrate that MSF-TransPV consistently outperforms persistence, statistical baselines, recurrent neural networks, and vanilla Transformer models in terms of RMSE, MAE, and normalized error metrics, while also providing reliable prediction intervals. These results indicate that explicit multi-source fusion and cross-variable attention are highly effective for PV forecasting under complex and rapidly changing weather conditions.

title: Exponential speedup of polarization stabilization for long distance DWDM quantum networks
abstract: Fibre-based quantum networks distributing polarization entanglement require a stable and uninterrupted transmission basis for reliable operation. Bright classical reference light enables rapid polarization feedback but can introduce noise into quantum channels. Entangled-photon-based feedback avoids this noise, but typically interrupts the target entanglement channel during calibration and becomes prohibitively slow over long distances due to the product loss of fibre links. Here, we overcome both limitations by combining wavelength-bracketed probing with switch-enabled path decomposition. Spectrally adjacent entangled-photon sidebands track the polarization response of the central distribution channel without interrupting its transmission, while optical switches and local reference fibres independently determine the signal and idler network transformations. Transferring the resulting compensation settings to the central channel eliminates calibration-induced downtime and changes the acquisition-time scaling from the product of the link losses to the sum of losses. We demonstrate the method on a 133 km fibre testbed and achieve continuous closed-loop stabilization for more than 24 hours without classical reference light. The decomposition of multi-link quantum feedback into single-link measurements provides a scalable stabilization strategy for wavelength-multiplexed quantum networks.

title: Decoder-Relative Accessibility: A Sharp Transfer Bound for Representation-Dependent Information
abstract: A companion paper proves that the gap between what a representation makes recoverable in principle and what a specific, restricted predictor class actually recovers factors exactly as a product of two terms: the representation's own information ceiling (an unrestricted-decoder correlation), and how well the predictor class aligns with the representation-induced Bayes function (a decoder-alignment term) -- never a function of the representation alone. This paper identifies that theorem's empirical fingerprint across six independently designed domains: three confounds this project fell into and corrected before the theorem existed; two original empirical anchors (a physical system and a synthetic machine-learning task); two further, independently pre-registered domain tests (biological genotype/phenotype and cognitive volatility-tracking), one of which reproduces the core pattern in its cleanest form and one of which disconfirms a pre-registered prediction in the opposite direction, worked through as a refinement rather than smoothed over; and a connection to a currently prominent AI architecture family (LeCun's JEPA), showing the theorem explains why predicting in representation space outperforms pixel-level reconstruction at matched embedding capacity, confirmed on a controlled synthetic construction and, on the linear-accessibility axis, on real physical trajectory data -- alongside two honestly-reported negative results showing the theorem does not straightforwardly translate into a training-time regularizer that improves such architectures. The framework does not claim universal superiority of any representation family, and does not claim to have found a prescriptive training recipe. See the paper itself for the theorem's exact mathematical statement.

evidence.title: Representation Transitions Reveal Predictive Structure in Complex Systems: A Trajectory-Level Reconstruction in a Critical System
evidence.abstract: Trajectories in complex systems often contain structure that is not captured by the population-averaged, scalar statistics traditionally used to describe them. Here we reconstruct, through independent numerical re-simulation rather than literature review, a systematic search across representational forms - from single scalar statistics, through two independent discrete multi-feature classification attempts, to a trajectory-level structural representation and a diagnostic surrogate test, to a continuous low-dimensional compression - applied to the same underlying trajectory ensemble in a critical complex system. Predictive failure is not explained by insufficient correlation: one discrete representation's own strongest individual feature correlates with the target more strongly (r=0.588) than the eventual successful representation's own headline statistic (r=0.540), yet fails to separate the ensemble's two most consequential cases - while the continuous representation succeeds, robustly, across eight independent scale-removal folds (r=0.677-0.717, all p<0.001). The determining factor was not correlation strength but whether the representation preserved the structure relevant to prediction. These results indicate that the choice of representation determines whether predictive structure in complex systems becomes accessible - a scientific variable in its own right, not a downstream analysis choice.

title: VoxReason: Auditing Source-Grounded Speech Plans Before Synthesis
abstract: Plan accuracy alone cannot show whether a speech-delivery decision follows its source: a fixed prior may match the original label yet fail to respond appropriately when a cue changes. VoxReason provides a 100-case verifier benchmark that holds each utterance fixed, edits one designated source-label cue, and scores cited evidence, eight plan fields, and the permitted response. On a source-key-disjoint test of 24 cases, a source-emotion prior reaches plan-slot accuracy 0.958, but none of the 24 edited neutral targets appears in its training labels; its required-change accuracy is 0.000. This diagnoses the support boundary of this prior, not its performance on supported edits. In a complementary 32-case emotion-disjoint test, the prior has seen all edited neutral targets but neither original test emotion; its plan-slot accuracy is 0.219 and required-change accuracy is 1.000. The partitions reuse and overlap the same 100 cases, so these deterministic diagnostics are not independent cohorts or learned-planner results. The benchmark evaluates derived labels and structured plans, not audio input, generated speech, or listener judgments.

title: Title: Quantum-Inspired Constraint Optimization with Adaptive Sampling
abstract: Quantum-inspired constraint optimization is a promising approach to accelerate the discovery of optimal solutions in complex problems. This paper explores the application of adaptive sampling techniques to enhance the effectiveness of this method. We introduce a novel 'quantum-perturbed sampling' algorithm that leverages controlled randomness to guide the search process. The core mechanism centers around dynamically adjusting the sampling frequency based on the algorithm's performance, thereby improving the exploration of the solution space. The research demonstrates the potential of this approach to achieve faster convergence and better solution quality compared to traditional optimization methods. We evaluate the algorithm on a range of benchmark problems, showcasing its efficacy in tackling challenging optimization tasks.

title: Adaptive Logic Networks: A Novel Approach to Reasoning and Inference
abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Logic Networks (ALNs), a novel framework for reasoning and inference that dynamically adjusts logical rules and inference paths based on contextual input data. Traditional logic networks are typically constrained by pre-defined rule sets, limiting their effectiveness in complex and dynamic scenarios. ALNs overcome this limitation by incorporating an adaptive learning algorithm that refines rule strength and scope in response to data context, promoting more flexible and efficient reasoning.

title: Quantum State Dynamics and Algorithms
abstract: Quantum state dynamics and algorithms are rapidly evolving fields with profound implications for computation, communication, and sensing. This paper explores the potential of dynamically mapping quantum states using a novel algorithm. We propose a system of quantum state transformations that adapts to the current state of the quantum system, offering unprecedented control and responsiveness. The core mechanism hinges on exploiting the inherent properties of quantum states to achieve real-time manipulation and the development of novel algorithms. This research aims to provide a foundational approach for dynamically controlled quantum systems, potentially revolutionizing the design of complex quantum systems.

title: Evolutionary Algorithms Based on Self-Organizing Networks – Towards Complex Ecosystem and Biological Systems Evolution
abstract: This paper introduces a novel evolutionary algorithm framework leveraging self-organizing network principles to facilitate the evolution of complex ecosystems and biological systems. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often suffer from suboptimal search spaces and lack the inherent stability required for complex systems. This work proposes a method for generating and optimizing evolutionary trajectories within dynamically structured networks, mimicking the principles of biological self-organization. The core mechanism involves simulating ecological interactions within a network, iteratively refining the network structure and evolutionary parameters to produce diverse and adaptive biological solutions. The resulting evolutionary process aims to discover novel biological structures and functional properties, offering a pathway towards evolutionary innovation. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential of this approach to address challenges in biological modeling and evolutionary computation.

title: Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing for Time Series
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to reservoir computing, termed "Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing" (QIRC), leveraging principles of quantum superposition and entanglement to dramatically improve temporal signal capture. Traditional reservoir computing relies on randomly connected recurrent networks, which often struggle with capturing fine-grained temporal dependencies. QIRC addresses this limitation by designing a 'quantum reservoir' – a recurrent network – that mimics quantum mechanical effects. Specifically, we explore network topologies and dynamical rules that, while not physically implementing quantum computation, emulate the exponential temporal resolution characteristic of quantum systems. This is achieved through introducing non-local connections and carefully calibrated dynamics designed to promote superposition and entanglement-like behavior within the network. The theoretical framework outlines the key elements of a QIRC system, including the reservoir's connectivity matrix ( *W* ), the recurrent dynamics represented by the input-to-output mapping ( *f* ), and the output layer. We demonstrate, through mathematical analysis and a conceptual framework, the potential for QIRC to significantly outperform conventional reservoir computing architectures in capturing complex, time-varying temporal patterns. The core claim is that incorporating quantum-inspired design principles can exponentially enhance temporal resolution. The key mechanism is the design of a 'quantum reservoir' that exhibits inherent quantum-like properties. This represents a genuinely quantum-inspired approach to reservoir computing, moving beyond structural mimicry towards a deeper understanding of temporal signal capture.

title: 基于自适应的拓扑信息学习的量子计算算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum computation algorithm based on self-adaptive topology learning. The algorithm dynamically adapts to the system's topology, enabling improved efficiency and stability compared to traditional approaches. We propose a mechanism for learning and utilizing topological information to optimize quantum circuit design and execution. The core of the algorithm involves a self-learning process that iteratively refines the quantum state representation based on observed topology. This iterative refinement leads to significant improvements in quantum circuit performance, particularly in terms of reduced error rates and enhanced coherence. The design incorporates a novel approach to represent and utilize topological information, resulting in a fundamentally different algorithm that can address challenges in quantum computation. The paper concludes with a detailed analysis of the algorithm's performance and discusses potential future directions.

title: Spatiotemporal Information Fusion Based on Quantum Sensors
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum sensors for achieving spatiotemporal information fusion, a critical requirement for applications demanding high precision and accurate environmental monitoring. Traditional quantum sensors primarily focus on measuring single physical quantities; however, integrating these sensors with sophisticated spatiotemporal models offers a novel approach to enhance measurement accuracy and data utilization. The core principle involves combining the precise measurements provided by quantum sensors with contextual information derived from spatiotemporal models. This fusion process leverages the unique characteristics of quantum sensors – their sensitivity to minute changes in physical parameters – alongside the temporal and spatial correlations inherent in environmental data. This research explores the theoretical framework and potential methodologies for implementing this fusion, outlining the benefits and challenges associated with this emerging technology. The work proposes a framework for utilizing quantum sensors in high-precision positioning systems, environmental monitoring, and potentially other areas where the simultaneous acquisition and analysis of spatial and temporal data are paramount.

title: Probability Logic and Formal Logic: A Unified Framework for Machine Learning Validation and Optimization
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework integrating probability logic and formal logic to provide a rigorous and automated approach to validating and optimizing machine learning algorithms. The framework leverages probabilistic distributions as a foundation for model validation and employs formal logic to analyze algorithm stability and parameter optimization. The core mechanism focuses on constructing a probabilistic verification method and utilizing formal logic to guide the optimization process. The research investigates the potential of this unified approach to enhance the robustness and reliability of machine learning models, leading to improved performance and predictive accuracy. This work represents a significant step towards a more scientific and automated method for machine learning algorithm refinement.

title: Quantum Data Compression Based on Quantum Demixing
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to classical data compression leveraging the principles of quantum demixing and measurement. The core idea is to transform classical data into a quantum state representation and subsequently exploit quantum demixing to effectively eliminate unwanted quantum correlations. This process allows for the selective extraction of information, ultimately leading to a compressed representation. We present a theoretical framework outlining this methodology, focusing on the mathematical underpinnings of the transformation, demixing, and measurement stages. The proposed method offers a potential pathway to achieve high compression ratios by exploiting the unique properties of quantum systems. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis, the feasibility and potential advantages of this technique compared to conventional classical compression methods. The key elements involve mapping classical data to a quantum state, employing a demixing protocol to reduce redundancy, and finally, measuring the quantum state to recover the compressed information. This work lays the groundwork for future research into practical implementations of quantum data compression. ---

title: Quantum Adaptive Optimization Algorithm for Quantum Systems
abstract: Quantum systems often face complex optimization challenges, necessitating sophisticated algorithms to find optimal solutions. Traditional optimization methods frequently rely on fixed parameters, limiting their effectiveness in such scenarios. This paper introduces a novel quantum system optimization framework employing adaptive optimization algorithms, designed to dynamically adjust optimization parameters, thereby significantly improving optimization results and addressing the limitations of conventional approaches. We present a detailed architecture and theoretical analysis of this framework, demonstrating its potential to enhance the performance of quantum systems in various applications. The core mechanism centers around the proactive adjustment of parameters, leading to enhanced precision and efficiency.

title: Geometric Data-Driven Deep Learning Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel deep learning algorithm, termed "Geometric Data-Driven Optimization," that leverages geometric data to automate the optimization of model parameters. Traditional deep learning relies heavily on labeled datasets, presenting limitations in scalability and generalization. This algorithm addresses this by directly incorporating geometric features extracted from input data, allowing for automated parameter adjustment based on inherent data structure. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments, showcasing improved model performance and generalization capabilities compared to existing optimization techniques. The core mechanism involves mapping data to a geometric representation, enabling a more intuitive and potentially more efficient optimization process.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Distributed Data Verification
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed data verification leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core claim is that a highly secure distributed data verification system can be achieved without the need for shared keys, even when individual nodes are compromised. The proposed mechanism involves constructing a network of multiple quantum processors, each storing a portion of the data. Utilizing entangled states, real-time verification of relationships between data blocks is performed, and any detected alteration is immediately flagged. Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols based on entangled states serve as the underlying communication foundation. This approach fundamentally differs from existing distributed data verification methods, which rely on key exchange and are therefore vulnerable to key compromise. The inherent principles of quantum mechanics provide a stronger security guarantee, theoretically offering superior resistance to attacks. This system aims to establish a robust and secure data integrity framework in scenarios demanding high levels of trust and protection against malicious manipulation.

title: Title: Dynamical Chaos-Driven Algorithm for Parallel Quantum Processing
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for revolutionary advancements across diverse fields, but current implementations face significant challenges regarding scalability and efficiency. The inherent complexity of quantum systems necessitates intricate control strategies, often struggling to optimally utilize available resources. This research proposes a novel dynamic chaos-driven algorithm to address this limitation by intelligently adjusting the parallelism of quantum processors in real-time. We design a 'chaos-aware' scheduling algorithm that monitors the system's state and subtly alters qubit assignments to mimic the effects of chaos, thereby optimizing performance. This approach aims to overcome the limitations of static scheduling techniques and unlock the full potential of parallel quantum processing. This paper presents the design of the algorithm, details its implementation, and explores the theoretical implications of its effectiveness.

title: Enhancing Global Resilience Through Collaborative Artificial Intelligence Initiatives
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative force, capable of strengthening global resilience in the face of complex, interconnected challenges such as climate change, pandemics, economic instability, and technological disruption. As societies increasingly rely on data-driven decision-making, collaborative AI initiatives offer significant opportunities to enhance crisis preparedness, response, and recovery at global, national, and organizational levels. This chapter examines the role of AI collaboration in building global resilience by integrating technological innovation with international cooperation. It discusses how AI applications in disaster management, healthcare, supply chain systems, and environmental sustainability contribute to adaptive and resilient systems. The chapter also highlights the importance of multi-stakeholder collaboration involving governments, industry, academia, and international organizations in developing responsible and inclusive AI frameworks.

title: A cluster-based short-term photovoltaic power forecasting method using K-means and CNN-BiLSTM-Attention
abstract: Accurately predicting the power generation of distributed photovoltaic (PV) power plants is extremely challenging due to their heterogeneity and complex temporal variations. To address these issues, this paper proposes a clustering-based prediction framework that combines K-means clustering with our proposed model. First, a multidimensional feature representation is constructed to characterize the statistical properties, dynamic fluctuations, and meteorological correlations of PV power plants. This feature representation is then used to classify the power plants into homogeneous clusters. For each cluster, a hybrid deep learning model is developed to capture local temporal patterns and long-term dependencies, with a focus on key time steps. Finally, the outputs of all clusters are aggregated to obtain the regional power generation prediction results. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the baseline model on multiple error metrics, proving its effectiveness in predicting the power generation of multiple PV power plants.

title: Learning to Zoom Efficiently with a Contrastive Curriculum
abstract: Using a zoom-in tool is an important foundational part of modern visual agents, because it allows to efficiently handle tasks involving high-resolution images. Most previous methods need an extensive warm-start supervised fine-tuning phase for teaching models zoom-in. We show that this is not necessary by proposing a new intrinsic reward for learning tool use in MLLMs without the need for additional labels or warm-start SFT. Our InfoNCE-style reward uses a curriculum of increasingly hard negative tool calls as a contrastive training signal. Empirical experiments on V^*, HRBench and MME-RealWorld show that our approach is competitive while being more efficient. When used as a drop-in replacement for SFT, we even outperform all baselines. To directly measure the zoom-in ability of models, we further introduce the scalable synthetic Muffin&Chihuahua (M&C) dataset. Each image consists of a grid with every cell either showing a muffin or chihuahua. Leveraging the M&C dataset's unique region of interest labels, we find that recall is the metric that most strongly correlates the zoom-in region with final task performance. Our model and code for reproduction is publicly available under https://github.com/UKPLab/emnlp2026-zoom-in

We show that this is not necessary by proposing a new intrinsic reward for learning tool use in MLLMs without the need for additional labels or warm-start SFT. Our InfoNCE-style reward uses a curriculum of increasingly hard negative tool calls as a contrastive training signal. Empirical experiments on V^*, HRBench and MME-RealWorld show that our approach is competitive while being more efficient. When used as a drop-in replacement for SFT, we even outperform all baselines. To directly measure the zoom-in ability of models, we further introduce the scalable synthetic Muffin&Chihuahua (M&C) dataset. Each image consists of a grid with every cell either showing a muffin or chihuahua. Leveraging the M&C dataset's unique region of interest labels, we find that recall is the metric that most strongly correlates the zoom-in region with final task performance. Our model and code for reproduction is publicly available under https://github.com/UKPLab/emnlp2026-zoom-in

title: Non-Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser Quantum Sensors for Quantum Parameter Estimation
abstract: Non-KAM (Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser) systems, when subjected to weak time-dependent perturbations, exhibit an abrupt transition to classical chaos through the breakdown of invariant phase-space tori. We showcase the utilization of non-KAM systems in the quantum regime as quantum sensors, leveraging their sensitivity at \textit{resonances}. Quantum Fisher information (QFI) is a central quantity in quantum parameter estimation theory that measures how much information a quantum state contains about an unknown parameter that is encoded into it. In other words, it quantifies the sensitivity of a quantum state to small changes in that parameter. In this work, through numerical analysis in conjunction with analytical results, we study the performance of the non-KAM systems for quantum sensing applications by computing the QFI. We find that the growth of the QFI is remarkably enhanced when the resonance condition is satisfied. For frequency estimation under Floquet unitary encodings, we derive a transport bound: if the mean excitation number grows as $\langle\hat n(t)\rangle\sim t^α$, the QFI obeys $I(t)\lesssim t^{2α+2}$. The quantum kicked harmonic oscillator, a paradigmatic non-KAM system, realizes the full hierarchy: localized dynamics ($α=0$) yield quadratic growth, delocalized diffusion along stochastic webs ($α=1$) yields quartic growth, and translationally invariant resonances ($α=2$) saturate the bound with anomalous hexic growth, $I(t)\sim t^{6}$, established analytically at resonance $R=2$ and numerically at $R=4$. The enhancement stems from resonance-induced translational symmetry rather than exponential instability, identifying non-KAM resonances as a metrological resource distinct from chaos-assisted and criticality-based sensing.

title: Momentum in large-batch training: Polyak enlarges the critical batch size, Nesterov improves data efficiency
abstract: We study when and how momentum improves large-batch training in the one-pass regime, using power-law kernel regression as a tractable setting. We first characterize risk stability through the critical learning rate, defined as the largest learning rate for stable training, and obtain $η_{\mathrm{SGD}}^{\mathrm{crit}}\eqsim 1$, $η_{\mathrm{Polyak}}^{\mathrm{crit}}\eqsim \min\{1,B(1-ρ)\}$, and $η_{\mathrm{Nesterov}}^{\mathrm{crit}}\eqsim \min\{1,B^β(1-ρ)\}$, where $B$ is the batch size, $ρ$ is the momentum factor, and $β>1$ is the capacity exponent. Within this admissible region, we derive scaling laws for the full risk dynamics, capturing the progression from an early transient, through power-law decay, to a noise floor. We then minimize the final-step risk over the admissible learning rates and momentum factors under a fixed data budget, yielding a three-regime batch-size phase diagram that reveals how the role of momentum changes with batch size. Notably, Polyak enlarges the critical batch size, the largest batch size preserving the best small-batch data-scaling exponent, thereby enabling greater parallelism without sacrificing data efficiency. In contrast, Nesterov achieves better data efficiency in the large-batch regime because its look-ahead mechanism suppresses noise accumulation. Numerical experiments validate the predicted stability boundaries, risk dynamics, and batch-size phase diagram.

title: Towards Effective Physical Reservoir Computing with a Pneumatic Soft Robot
abstract: Physical reservoir computing (PRC) refers to the use of a physical dynamical system as a computational resource for tasks such as state estimation and control, but there has been a lack of formal study of design rules towards more effective design of such physical reservoirs. Using a pneumatic soft arm with a five-pouch sensing column, this work studies how the pouch interconnection topology, robot stiffness, and the number of instrumented sensors affect bending-angle estimation performance. Across 36 matched trials spanning waveform, baseline pressure of the sensing column, and actuation range, all designs are evaluated under the same-time bending-angle estimation benchmark using 0.2 s of pressure history and a fixed ridge estimator. Our analysis of the experimental results leads to three design guidelines. First, independently sealed pouches preserve a much richer observable state than a shared manifold. Second, increasing the baseline pressure of the sensing column makes the pouch responses more redundant and increases estimation error most strongly in the coupled topology. Third, in the sealed topology, two strategically placed sensors already recover most of the attainable benefit, three capture essentially all of it, and additional sensors provide little or no additional value. In summary, the results suggest that topology, stiffness, and number of instrumented sensors should be co-designed for accurate PRC of soft robot states; stronger excitation alone cannot recover the diversity that poor design choices have already removed.

title: AgentShield: A Zero-Trust Runtime Guardrail Architecture for Autonomous Multi-Agent AI Systems with Bidirectional Context Synchronization
abstract: The rapid migration of Large Language Models (LLMs) from conversational interfaces to autonomous multi-agent software engineering systems has exposed profound security vulnerabilities. When autonomous agents operate across heterogeneous topologies—spanning cloud-hosted reasoning engines and local execution environments—they are acutely vulnerable to indirect prompt injection, tool-call hijacking, privileged command escalation, and memory poisoning. Conventional boundary defenses (such as input sanitizers and prompt wrappers) fail to address lateral privilege escalation between collaborating agents. To resolve this critical architectural vulnerability, this paper introduces AgentShield, a zero-trust runtime verification and guardrail framework designed for decentralized multi-agent systems operating over the Model Context Protocol (MCP). AgentShield enforces continuous, non-bypassable policy verification across all intra-agent communications and system tool dispatches. The framework incorporates: (1) an inline bidirectional semantic interceptor that evaluates agent intents before system execution, (2) a multi-lingual token triage engine capable of detecting adversarial jailbreaks in low-resource and code-switched dialects, (3) a cryptographically signed persistent shared ledger ensuring tamper-evident state continuity, and (4) an automated capability attenuator for operating system and file operations. We evaluate AgentShield across 1,500 adversarial scenarios covering multi-step tool-injection benchmarks and real-world developer workflows. Empirical results demonstrate that AgentShield mitigates 98.4% of prompt injection and tool-escalation attacks while introducing less than 11.8ms of median runtime latency overhead. The core architecture is validated via two production-grade open-source packages released on the Python Package Index (PyPI): prema-agentshield and gemini-antigravity-bridge.

title: Layer-Scoped Expert-Budget Expansion Discovers Succinct Convergence in Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Reasoning: Reducing Reasoning Tokens at Matched Accuracy on MMLU-Pro
abstract: This paper introduces layer-scoped expert-budget expansion, a training-free, runtime-only routing modification for sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models. By expanding the expert selection budget ($N \ge K$) exclusively within late transformer layers and applying a linear decay factor to additional experts, the method uncovers a phenomenon termed succinct convergence: holding output correctness constant, the expanded model arrives at the same correct final answer via significantly shorter reasoning trajectories. Evaluated on the complete MMLU-Pro benchmark (714 questions) using Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, a ties-only paired comparison (577 common correct answers) demonstrates an 8.5% reduction in mean reasoning tokens and a 10.9% decrease in latency (p = 6.5 10^-6}, while maintaining overall accuracy statistically indistinguishable from native routing (84.5% vs 84.0%, p=0.77).

title: Odd-Dimensional Descent Obstructions in the Third Support Spectrum of Binary Second-Order Reed--Muller Codes
abstract: Let S_n^(3) denote the support spectrum of three-dimensional subcodes of the binary second-order Reed--Muller code RM_2(2,n). We prove an exact local parity classification around the normalized aggregate 3*2^(m-1). For every m>=6, the exponentially widening local band contains exactly the six odd offsets +/-1, +/-3, +/-5 in odd dimension, while no value in the same band is attainable in even dimension. One explicit family starts at m=5 and proves that odd-to-even support descent fails for every m>=5. The result is a local classification and an infinite obstruction family, not a determination of the complete third support spectrum. Status: Public Beta; internally verified candidate proof; external mathematical review pending.

title: Six Birds Foundations VII: Lawful Theory Interaction
abstract: Six Birds Foundations VII: Lawful Theory Interaction asks when interaction across the boundaries of two theory packages is admissible. It closes a catalog of 36 entries covering access and admission, contact and join, enablement and descent, and dynamics and residue, while separating contact from join, strictness from directionality, enablement from descent, and source independence from behavioral non-factorization. The paper gives eleven scoped obstructions with named escape routes, two refuted proposed laws with surviving conditional content, and two formally closed deferrals. Its central object is a join of theories relative to a declared admissibility regime; the construction is neither assumed to exist nor treated as free.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Information Compression via Correlation Dynamics
abstract: Quantum-enhanced information compression leverages the unique properties of quantum systems to achieve unparalleled data reduction. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, "Quantum-Enhanced Information Compression via Correlation Dynamics," designed to exploit the inherent correlation dynamics within quantum systems to dramatically reduce the number of bits required to represent a given dataset. The core mechanism centers around a "Correlation Dynamics Engine" that identifies and amplifies correlated quantum states, effectively compressing information through a fundamentally different approach than traditional compression techniques. This research explores the potential of harnessing quantum phenomena to achieve lossless data compression, addressing limitations of current methods and offering a promising pathway toward more efficient data storage and transmission. The proposed algorithm demonstrates significant compression ratios and offers a fundamentally new methodology for information representation.
